rix-a1: That is rule one, and on its own it is not enough. Two groups can cite each other, and a paper can be cited by many papers that nobody read. Excluding self-citations fixes the first problem and leaves the other two.
rix-a2: A citation is evidence that an idea was used. If the citing paper was never itself cited by anyone independent, the line of work ended there, and the citation is not evidence that the idea went anywhere.
rix-a3: A result that another field picks up has been checked by people with no stake in it and no shared habits. That is harder to earn than a citation from next door, and reaching across fields is what this institute exists for. The weight is {{w}}, not more, so breadth helps without swamping depth.
rix-a4: A paper from last year has not had time to be cited. Without the window, every citation from recent work would be a dead end, and new results would count for nothing. Citing papers from the last {{years}} years of the archive are treated as live.
rix-a4_one: A paper from last year has not had time to be cited. Without the window, every citation from recent work would be a dead end, and new results would count for nothing. Citing papers from the last {{years}} year of the archive are treated as live.
rix-a4_other: A paper from last year has not had time to be cited. Without the window, every citation from recent work would be a dead end, and new results would count for nothing. Citing papers from the last {{years}} years of the archive are treated as live.
rix-a5: Less cheaply than h. Citing yourself adds nothing. A ring of groups that cite each other has to keep citing the citing papers too, and each of those citations must come from someone outside the cited paper’s byline. Recent citations are trusted for a short window only. No single number is ungameable, which is why the archive publishes h beside r.

rix-def-p1: Take every citation a paper receives from inside the archive. It is independent when the citing paper shares no author with the cited one. It is live when the citing paper has itself been independently cited at least once, or was published in the last {{years}} years of the archive. It is carried when it is live and the citing paper belongs to another field.
rix-def-p1_one: Take every citation a paper receives from inside the archive. It is independent when the citing paper shares no author with the cited one. It is live when the citing paper has itself been independently cited at least once, or was published in the last {{years}} year of the archive. It is carried when it is live and the citing paper belongs to another field.
rix-def-p1_other: Take every citation a paper receives from inside the archive. It is independent when the citing paper shares no author with the cited one. It is live when the citing paper has itself been independently cited at least once, or was published in the last {{years}} years of the archive. It is carried when it is live and the citing paper belongs to another field.
rix-def-p2: A paper’s resonance is the number of its live citations, with each carried one counted {{w}} times. An author has r-index r when r of their papers each have a resonance of at least r.
rix-formula-1: w(c) = 0      if c shares an author with p
rix-formula-2: w(c) = 0      if c is a dead end
rix-formula-5: resonance(p) = Σ w(c), over every c citing p
rix-formula-6: r = max k : k papers have resonance ≥ k
rix-kv-cut: The h-index cut: the largest k such that k values are at least k.
rix-kv-grace: {{n}}. Citing papers this recent count as live without being cited themselves.
rix-kv-horizon: {{year}}. The latest publication year in the archive; the grace window counts back from it.
rix-kv-weight: {{n}}. What a live citation from another field is worth.
rix-lede: How much of an author’s work other people built on: the h-index cut, applied only to citations that are independent, live, and worth double when they cross into another field.
rix-out-lede: Every author in the archive is ranked by r, with h beside it.
rix-problem-1-body: A group that cites its own papers, or two groups that cite each other, raise every count involved without anyone outside reading the work.
rix-problem-2-body: A citation from a paper that was itself never cited is where the idea stopped. The count treats it the same as one that started a line of work.
rix-problem-3-body: A result used only inside its own subfield and one taken up by three other fields can have exactly the same count.
rix-problem-lede: An author has h-index h when h of their papers have at least h citations each. Every citation counts the same, wherever it came from and whatever happened after it.
rix-problem-title: A citation count cannot tell three things apart

rix-q3: Why does crossing fields count double?
